correctness.rationale: The proof first matches entire zero-color Boolean fibers; the unmatched total-dominating faces form an upward-closed filter whose cover incidences preserve occupied nonzero-color support. At most two monochromatic occupied runs fit in seven positions. All resulting one-/two-color sector posets are precisely the 29/28-state finite enumerations, independent of n, with acyclic matchings and respectively one degree-four and one degree-three plus one degree-four critical cell. The exact signed two-color Morse differential is (-1)+(+1)=0, and other degree-four to degree-three incidences are barred by sector separation. Thus the universal Morse CW complex has one zero-cell, binomial(n-1,2) degree-three and binomial(n,2) degree-four cells with zero integral attaching-degree matrix. By Hurewicz all degree-four attachments are nullhomotopic. Replaying the standalone standard-library checker verifies finite sector acyclicity, integer coefficient zero and independent full-complex calculations for n=2..5. No finite-to-infinite extrapolation is used; the reduction is uniform. Boundary conventions and n=2 are explicit.

originality.rationale: Antolín Camarena and Carnero Bravo 2023 Theorem 23 allows possible Moore torsion at cycle length seven and Question 24 asks for torsion-freeness; the finite n=3,4,5 examples they report do not entail a uniform formula. An indexed C7 x K4 wedge result and prior single-n symmetry calculations cover individual parameter values only. The later 2025 path-factor work and 2026 generalized Mycielskian work concern different constructions. A search across categorical/direct/Kronecker product terminology, precise binomial ranks, the 29/28-sector method, and all-color formulations revealed no result logically implying the theorem. The new claim is the uniform n>=2 identification, not its previously known cases.

value.rationale: The precise object C7 x Kn lies in a published torsion open problem. The finding settles its entire seven-cycle infinite branch and upgrades two-consecutive-degree homology with possible Moore spaces to an integral wedge-of-spheres classification with exact binomial ranks. The parameter-independent reduction is structural, its boundary cancellation is integral, and it has direct use as a base family for studying torsion and graph product topology at other cycle lengths. The result is neither a fixed-size table recomputation nor a routine substitution.
